masteryZone.q: Who is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India?
masteryZone.sol: M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India. He developed high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds for wheat and rice.

masteryZone.q: The Green Revolution in India started in which year?
masteryZone.sol: The Green Revolution started in India in 1965 with the introduction of HYV seeds, particularly in Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh.

masteryZone.q: Which crops were the main focus of the Green Revolution?
masteryZone.sol: The Green Revolution mainly focused on wheat and rice production through HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following states benefited most from the Green Revolution? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh benefited most from the Green Revolution due to better irrigation facilities and infrastructure.

masteryZone.q: The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in all food crops.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in wheat and rice, but India still imports pulses, edible oils, and other nutri-cereals.

masteryZone.f: HYV seeds can produce higher yields without adequate irrigation and fertilizers.
masteryZone.sol: False. HYV seeds require adequate irrigation, chemical fertilizers, and other inputs to achieve higher yields.

masteryZone.q: The Green Revolution started in India in the year ______.
masteryZone.sol: The Green Revolution started in India in 1965 with the introduction of HYV seeds.

masteryZone.q: M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the ______ Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India.

masteryZone.q: What does HYV stand for?
masteryZone.sol: HYV stands for High-Yielding Variety seeds.

masteryZone.q: Name one negative impact of the Green Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: Groundwater depletion, soil degradation, increased use of chemical fertilizers, regional disparities, or neglect of millets and pulses.

masteryZone.q: Who is known as the Father of the White Revolution?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Verghese Kurien is known as the Father of the White Revolution. He founded Amul and pioneered the cooperative dairy movement.

masteryZone.q: Operation Flood was launched by which organization?
masteryZone.sol: Operation Flood was launched by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) in 1970 under the leadership of Dr. Verghese Kurien.

masteryZone.q: The Anand Pattern is associated with which sector?
masteryZone.sol: The Anand Pattern is the three-tier cooperative dairy model developed by Dr. Kurien at Anand, Gujarat.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are features of the cooperative dairy model? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The cooperative model eliminates middlemen, is farmer-led, and has a three-tier structure. It was replicated nationwide, not limited to Gujarat.

masteryZone.q: India is the world's largest milk producer due to the White Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: True. The White Revolution (Operation Flood) made India the world's largest milk producer, increasing production from 20 million tonnes (1970) to 180+ million tonnes.

masteryZone.q: Operation Flood was entirely a government scheme implemented by bureaucrats.
masteryZone.sol: False. Operation Flood was a farmer-led cooperative movement, with NDDB providing technical support. It was spearheaded by farmers themselves.

masteryZone.q: Operation Flood was implemented in ______ phases.
masteryZone.sol: Operation Flood was implemented in three phases from 1970 to 1996.

masteryZone.q: NDDB stands for National ______ Development Board.
masteryZone.sol: NDDB stands for National Dairy Development Board.

masteryZone.q: What is the Anand Pattern in dairy development?
masteryZone.sol: A three-tier cooperative structure: Village Dairy Cooperative Societies → District Milk Unions → State Dairy Federations.

masteryZone.q: How did the White Revolution empower rural women?
masteryZone.sol: It created employment opportunities in dairy cooperatives and gave women economic independence through milk sales.

masteryZone.q: The Blue Revolution is related to which sector?
masteryZone.sol: The Blue Revolution is related to fisheries and aquaculture production, making India the second-largest fish producer.

masteryZone.q: Yellow Revolution focused on increasing production of:
masteryZone.sol: The Yellow Revolution (1986-1990) focused on increasing edible oil production through mustard, sunflower, and soybean.

masteryZone.q: The Golden Revolution is associated with:
masteryZone.sol: The Golden Revolution (1991-2003) focused on horticulture - increasing production of fruits, vegetables, flowers, and honey.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are color revolutions in India? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Green, White, and Blue are recognized color revolutions. Red Revolution is not a recognized agricultural revolution in India.

masteryZone.q: The Yellow Revolution was launched to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oils.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Yellow Revolution (1986-1990) aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in edible oils to reduce imports.

masteryZone.q: India is the largest fish producer in the world due to the Blue Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: False. India is the second-largest fish producer in the world. China is the largest.

masteryZone.q: The ______ Revolution is associated with horticulture and honey production.
masteryZone.sol: The Golden Revolution (1991-2003) focused on horticulture and honey production.

masteryZone.q: The National Horticulture Mission promoted the ______ Revolution.
masteryZone.sol: The National Horticulture Mission promoted the Golden Revolution.

masteryZone.q: What is the Blue Revolution?
masteryZone.sol: The Blue Revolution refers to the enhancement of fisheries and aquaculture production in India.

masteryZone.q: Who is known as the Father of the Blue Revolution?
masteryZone.sol: Hiralal Chaudhuri is known as the Father of the Blue Revolution in India.

masteryZone.q: e-NAM stands for:
masteryZone.sol: e-NAM (Electronic National Agriculture Market) is an online trading platform launched in 2016 to integrate APMC markets across India.

masteryZone.q: PM-KISAN scheme provides:
masteryZone.sol: PM-KISAN provides direct income support of Rs. 6000 per year to small and marginal farmers.

masteryZone.q: Contract farming was promoted after:
masteryZone.sol: Contract farming was promoted after the economic reforms of 1991 and India's entry into the WTO.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are recent agricultural initiatives? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: e-NAM, PM-KISAN, and Soil Health Card are recent initiatives. Green Revolution started in 1965.

masteryZone.q: India's entry into WTO brought changes to agricultural subsidies.
masteryZone.sol: True. The WTO Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) led to reduction in agricultural subsidies and pushed for export-oriented agriculture.

masteryZone.q: The Green Revolution had no environmental consequences.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Green Revolution led to groundwater depletion, soil degradation, and increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides.

masteryZone.q: ______ is an online trading platform for agricultural commodities launched in 2016.
masteryZone.sol: e-NAM (Electronic National Agriculture Market) was launched in 2016.

masteryZone.q: PM-KISAN provides Rs. ______ per year to farmers.
masteryZone.sol: PM-KISAN provides Rs. 6000 per year in three installments to small and marginal farmers.

masteryZone.q: What is the main purpose of the Soil Health Card scheme?
masteryZone.sol: To provide soil testing and nutrient management recommendations to farmers for better productivity.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1991 economic reforms affect agriculture?
masteryZone.sol: They reduced fertilizer subsidies, promoted contract farming, encouraged private investment, and pushed for agro-exports.
